propositions: A model class configured with provider="bedrock" and a canonical versioned Bedrock model id containing a colon has its explicit provider silently dropped because _resolve_target treats any colon in the model string as already provider-qualified.
infer_provider mis-splits a versioned Bedrock id on the first colon, yielding a fragment of the model id (e.g. 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') that the provider factory rejects.

The failure surfaces late as an 'unknown provider' error naming most of the model id, contradicting the operator's own config since bedrock IS registered, and degrading the review gate to INDETERMINATE/BLOCK.
Only unversioned Bedrock aliases without a colon happened to resolve correctly, which masked the bug from existing tests.

The fix centralizes the qualified/unqualified decision in one helper split_provider_qualifier used by both _resolve_target and infer_provider, deciding by prefix shape (identifier with no dots) rather than mere colon presence.

Graceful fallback to a default provider is explicitly rejected because silent substitution defeats the epic's purpose of guaranteeing the configured provider is used; the gate must fail closed and ideally fail fast at config time.
